> **A note on evaluation.** The code in this vignette is shown for illustration
> and is **not executed** when the vignette is built. A realistic bootstrap run
> is too slow for automated checks, so no output is embedded here; copy the
> chunks into an interactive session to reproduce the results locally.

## 1  Why reproducibility is the point

Bootstrap covariate selection answers a question single-fit summaries cannot: if
we resampled the study, would we keep choosing the same covariates? That
reassurance is only meaningful if the procedure is itself reproducible — the same
seed must yield the same answer today, tomorrow, and regardless of whether the
replicates run on one core or many. In this vignette we run a bootstrap SCM over
the bundled `demo_eres` cohort, inspect inclusion probabilities, and show how a
single seed now delivers identical resamples in both sequential and parallel
execution. We also flag an important consequence of that change: results
generated by earlier package versions will not reproduce here, and we point the
reader to where that break is documented.

This vignette focuses on the reproducibility guarantee. For the interpretation of
inclusion probabilities, co-inclusion matrices, and modal models, see
`vignette("bootstrap-stability", package = "erSCM")`.

## 2  Setup and an initial fit

```{r load}
library(erSCM)
data("demo_eres")

demo_eres <- demo_eres |>
  dplyr::mutate(SEX = as.factor(SEX))

fit_glm <- scm_glm(
  eres_data          = demo_eres,
  exposure_vars      = "CMAXss",
  covariates         = c("WT", "AGE", "EGFR", "ALB", "SEX"),
  dv_col             = "sim_status",
  significance_level = c(0.05, 0.01),
  center             = TRUE
)
```

## 3  A seeded bootstrap

`scm_bootstrap()` takes the fitted object and re-runs the entire SCM procedure on
each resample. The `seed` argument fixes the random-number stream.

```{r boot-seq}
stability <- scm_bootstrap(fit_glm, n_boot = 200, seed = 42)

print(stability)
```

Every replicate draws its resample from a dedicated, seed-derived stream. Running
the call a second time with the same seed reproduces the inclusion probabilities
exactly.

```{r boot-seq-again}
stability_again <- scm_bootstrap(fit_glm, n_boot = 200, seed = 42)

identical(
  stability$inclusion_probability,
  stability_again$inclusion_probability
)
```

## 4  Sequential and parallel agree

The key property is that parallel execution does not change the answer. Under the
hood each replicate is assigned the same per-replicate stream whether the
replicates are evaluated sequentially or dispatched across worker processes, so a
given `seed` produces the same resamples in both modes.

To run in parallel, register a parallel backend with `future::plan()` before
calling `scm_bootstrap(..., parallel = TRUE)`:

```{r boot-par}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)

stability_par <- scm_bootstrap(fit_glm, n_boot = 200, seed = 42, parallel = TRUE)

identical(
  stability$inclusion_probability,
  stability_par$inclusion_probability
)

future::plan(future::sequential)
```

Because the two modes share the same stream assignment, the sequential and
parallel inclusion probabilities match to the bit, and one can develop a workflow
sequentially and then scale it out for a confirmatory `n_boot = 1000` run without
altering the result.

## 5  A note on version compatibility

The unified per-replicate stream assignment changed how seeds map to resamples.
As a result, **bootstrap outputs produced by earlier versions of `erSCM` will not
reproduce under the current version**, even with the same `seed`. This is an
intentional correctness fix rather than a regression; the change is recorded in
`NEWS.md`. When comparing against archived results, re-run the bootstrap under the
current version rather than expecting the old numbers to reappear.

## 6  Interactions stay hierarchy-respecting

When the search includes interaction terms, each replicate only tests an
interaction once both of its parent main effects are present. Requesting
main-effects-only behaviour keeps spurious interaction terms out of every
replicate:

```{r boot-cox}
fit_cox <- scm_coxph(
  eres_data          = demo_eres,
  exposure_vars      = "CMAXss",
  covariates         = c("WT", "AGE"),
  dv_col             = "sim_status",
  time_col           = "sim_time",
  significance_level = c(0.05, 0.01),
  center             = TRUE
)

stability_cox <- scm_bootstrap(fit_cox, n_boot = 200, seed = 42)

print(stability_cox)
```

The same seeded, reproducible machinery applies to the Cox proportional-hazards
endpoint.
